profile_text.body:
Serve Robotics Inc. /DE/ is a public company headquartered in San Carlos, California, traded under the ticker SERV, with SEC CIK 0001832483. On its own website the company describes itself as building self-driving robots for last-mile delivery, framing the pitch around the question of why a 2-pound burrito should move in a 2-ton car. It calls its robots a low-emissions solution to the last-mile problem and says it is setting a standard for safety on and beyond the sidewalk, including protecting customer data, employees, and the public.

The site presents the robots as an established presence rather than a pilot: it says Serve Robotics is already a pop culture icon, and notes that one of its robots, Saymo, appears as John Mulaney's sidekick on the show "Everybody's Live" when not delivering burritos. That is the extent of the product and AI detail the company's own pages provide here, describing autonomous sidewalk delivery rather than any named model, platform, or software product.

The company's legal record shows no lawsuits listed. Its recorded legal exposure sits in California.
